slots.hypothesis: The reward applies its EMA to the raw values, and raw minute-return kurtosis is extremely heavy-tailed (about +236 on a day with one traded minute). So the head's EMA20 is really a memory of whether any spike day happened in the last month, and spike days can come from sparse trading, a coarse price grid on low-priced stocks, limit locks and jumps, or true tail shape. The core itself goes into the controls, so a monotone rewrite or a new smoothing window cannot score. The 16 seeds try three outer treatments, each with at least 2 operators where possible: (1) remove the suspected confounds by ranking within zero-ratio or nominal-price deciles, taking cross-sectional rank-regression residuals, and taking time-series residuals on the stock's own intraday volatility and turnover; (2) change the aggregation over days to a 60-day median, a 40-day lower-quartile tail mean, a slow EMA of daily ranks, and cross_madz (how unusual today is); (3) relate the core to trading with its 20-day correlation to turnover, kurtosis times skew, and the rank gap between return kurtosis and turnover kurtosis.

Kurtosis treats the 241 minute returns as an unordered sample and ignores how much money traded in each minute. None of the five controls carries order or trade-timing information either. Three lines: (a) order and price efficiency through AR(1), Durbin-Watson and Hurst on minute returns; (b) trade-volume clock versus wall clock through amount-weighted volatility over clock volatility, the mean return of the heaviest 10% of minutes, the turnover centroid, whether turnover is back-loaded, and turnover timing minus volatility timing; (c) price-volume dependence through same-minute and lagged correlations of returns with amount, the close-volume correlation, and signed-turnover share. 16 seeds, all scale-free intraday statistics whose skeletons differ from day_kurt.

result.predictions:
E: about 40% chance of producing heads (1-2 if any). The likeliest source is the 'how unusual today is' family (cross_madz, or cross_regres on the stock's own volatility or turnover), with a chosen half-life of 0 or 5, not 20. Most bucket and cross-sectional-regression seeds should score below 0.3; if one of them reaches 0.5 or more, true tail shape (H2) has independent alpha. The GP may drift toward core plus an unrelated good branch. The c05_periphery_seen refusal count should stay below 5.
N: about 65% chance of 1-3 heads, most likely from the price-volume correlation branch or the signed-turnover share. AR(1)/DW alone is unlikely to pass because the liquidity control absorbs most of it, and Hurst is probably noise. Any head should have residual |rho| below 0.3 with day_kurt(Ret).
R: zero-ratio EMA passes the gates with rho_head of 0.5 or more (I expect 0.5-0.8). Nominal price has rho_head between 0.3 and 0.6, long the high-priced names. Kurtosis on traded minutes only, and kurtosis of 5-minute returns, both score below 0.7. At least one of the cs_rank, log(kurt+5) and median variants beats 0.97, but the chance of an actual replacement is about 35%. gini has rho_head of 0.5 or more but misses the +0.1 line. The limit-lock and scale-free MAX variants have rho_head below 0.5. 0-2 variants fail the gates. Replacements this round: 0 or 1.

From the source code: price fields are back-adjusted, so I measure nominal price as `log(div(day_sum(Amt), day_sum(Volume)))`.
